text:
incident-bot: Paging @sre-oncall — multiple GPU driver resets observed in cluster `prod-gpu-us-west-2`. Alert: 14 resets across 6 nodes in last 5m. Possible ECC/Xid activity. Creating incident INC-2026-421.

sre-oncall: on it. looking at node list now. thanks for the ping.

maria: which customers hit? any 5xxs showing in gateway? :eyes:

kai: seeing elevated tail latency on model-serving routes for a subset of requests, some client retries. Not universal.

devin: logs from runtime show repeated `Xid 31` then `Xid 35` followed by container crashes. grabbing nv-support logs.

ops-bot: Node summary: n-gpu-12 (x2 resets), n-gpu-15 (x3), n-gpu-18 (x1), n-gpu-21 (x4), n-gpu-29 (x2), n-gpu-33 (x2).

maria: ok. can we isolate affected capacity? prefer cordon/drain to avoid customer errors.

sre-oncall: agree. Starting cordon on n-gpu-21 and n-gpu-15 to stop new pods. Will drain gracefully.

kai: FYI some pods are pinned to those nodes by nodeSelector for model-ttl=low-latency. We'll need fallback routing to spare capacity.

devin: putting a temporary routing rule to avoid those nodes: console -> routing -> sticky exclude for `node:n-gpu-*` pattern.

sre-oncall: drain started on n-gpu-21. Draining shows 8 pods to evict, some stuck in terminating due to heavy GPU memory persisting.

maria: any OOM logs? memory corruption? :thinking_face:

devin: found repeated kernel messages on n-gpu-21:

```
[ 54321.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID: 4321, GPU was a hang. GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 54321.123458] GPU ECC error detected on GPU 0: single-bit ECC at mem 0x7f4a... fail_count=3
[ 54321.123460] containerd: container crashed: exit status 137
```

kai: Xid 31 + ECC single-bit could indicate escalating hardware errors. Need to check ECC counters across node fleet.

ops-bot: Running ECC counter query -> returning elevated corrected errors on n-gpu-15 and n-gpu-21. n-gpu-33 shows transient spikes.

frank: is there a known firmware/driver mismatch? recent kernel bump last week.

devin: kernel version 6.2.18, nvidia-driver 540.80.02 on affected nodes. Non-affected nodes run same versions, but affected ones show higher ucodes.

elaine: recommend quick isolation: cordon/evict, then reboot node to clear ECC state and driver. Schedule firmware check after stabilization.

maria: agree. Are there customer-facing incidents created? I'll notify CS for customers using low-latency tiers.

sre-oncall: taking ownership for mitigation steps. Plan: 1) finish draining n-gpu-21 and n-gpu-15, 2) reboot those nodes, 3) monitor metrics and routing fallback, 4) if resets persist, repro on staging and open support case with NVIDIA.

devin: temp mitigation: reduce batch size and enable aggressive KV prefix cache on routed instances to shift load off GPUs.

kai: updating dashboards: add tile showing Xid events by node and ECC corrected/uncorrected counts. Also adding alert for Xid>5/min per node.

ops-bot: Drain complete on n-gpu-21. Rebooting node n-gpu-21 now.

sre-oncall: reboot successful, node back in Ready after 90s. Observability: resets stopped on that node.

maria: what's status on n-gpu-15? any customers still impacted?

sre-oncall: n-gpu-15 drain in progress, 6/6 pods evicted. Rebooting n-gpu-15.

devin: while reboots happening, I'm running `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots and collecting kernel dmesg for all affected nodes to attach to INC-2026-421.

kai: noticed a pattern: most Xid events occur after sustained long requests >8s and with sequence lengths >1024. Could be thermal/steady-state memory bit flips under sustained load.

frank: we should lower per-token concurrency per GPU until postmortem. Throttle policy option available in runtime config.

sre-oncall: applied throttle to low-latency pool: concurrency cap 6 -> 4. Monitoring.

ops-bot: n-gpu-15 rebooted, back Ready. Observability shows transient ECC corrections but no new Xid after reboot for 10m.

maria: CS: proactively notified 3 accounts (acme, zonalytics, teal-ai) of potential brief degradations; support ticket links: <https://support.reed/INC-2026-421|INC-2026-421>

devin: collected logs attached to incident: `/var/log/nvidia/driver-collect-n-gpu-21.tar.gz`.

sre-oncall: verifying canary traffic: small percentage of traffic resumed to previously cordoned nodes via canary routing -> healthy.

kai: still seeing elevated corrected ECC counts on n-gpu-33, but no crashes yet. Flagging for hardware swap if persists.

elaine: creating HW swap ticket for n-gpu-21 and n-gpu-15 for next maintenance window. Tagging `hw-replace`.

maria: any suggestion for long-term mitigation? is automated node rotation for ECC spikes feasible?

devin: yes — propose runbook: if ECC corrected >100/hour or Xid>=3 in 10m then automatically cordon + notify oncall and start node rotate. Filing RFC in eng-infra.

sre-oncall: handoff to night oncall @maria in 30m. I'll leave incident in monitoring state, assign INC-2026-421 to infra.

maria: taking handoff. I'll keep watch and escalate to SOC if uncorrected ECC shows up. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-421 updated: status -> monitoring. Handed off from `sre-oncall` to `maria`. Timeline notes appended.

maria: final notes for handoff: action items - monitor Xid alerts, watch n-gpu-33 for spikes, follow HW-swap ticket ENG-OPS-1298, update CS with any customer-visible impact. If Xid resumes, escalate to vendor support and consider driver rollback to 535.x.

sre-oncall: thanks — dropping out. :wave:

maria: copied. I'll post postmortem stub after 24h stability check. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
